# release-doi

> A Claude Code skill (documentation-only, MIT, no tagged release yet) that runs the release workflow for DOI-registered research repositories following the identifier-federation triplet from [`authorship-strategy`](https://github.com/shimo4228/authorship-strategy) (ADRs 0001-0003) and its intrinsic-identifier layer (ADR-0013: Software Heritage archival + SWHID recording). Pre-flight Zenodo opt-in check + four-phase runbook + one post-release phase, preventing the most common release-time drift incidents (off-by-one concept-vs-version DOI canonicalization, missed sibling cross-reference updates, version DOI used where the concept DOI belongs, opt-in lag on first release of a new DOI repository). It also covers editing the metadata of an already published Zenodo record without a new version.

Status: active, synced one way from the author's Claude Code harness by `scripts/sync-from-local.sh` (it never commits); changes are collected under Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md.

## Core documentation

- [SKILL.md](skills/release-doi/SKILL.md): full skill specification (written in Japanese) — Pre-flight Zenodo opt-in check, four-phase runbook (Baseline, Cross-document consistency, Verify, Release execution), post-release phase (DOI minting wait, version DOI written into citation fields, SWHID recording, follow-up commit), published-record metadata edit (retrofit without a new version), recovery runbook for missed initial deposit
- [README.md](README.md): human-facing narrative (when to use, install, how it works, key concept, related skills)
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): release notes (Unreleased only; parts of it still describe an earlier five-phase layout)
- [inspiration.md](inspiration.md): the motivating incident

## Workflow phases

0. **Pre-flight: Zenodo opt-in check** — verify the Zenodo GitHub webhook is registered on the target repository via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/hooks`; the integration is repo-by-repo opt-in and not retroactive, so this gate catches missing toggles on first release of a new DOI repository
1. **Baseline** — capture pre-release ground truth from command output (commits since the last tag, file and test counts where applicable, the version in `pyproject.toml` and `CITATION.cff`, latest tags)
2. **Cross-document consistency** — opens with `/context-sync` for drift detection, then syncs CHANGELOG / CITATION.cff / `codemeta.json` / .zenodo.json / `pyproject.toml` / multilingual README / llms.txt / glossary / ADR bidirectional links
3. **Verify** — CITATION.cff schema and syntax (`uvx cffconvert --validate`), version triple, lint and test pass, secret scan, unintended-file check
4. **Release execution** — stage specific files, commit with the message passed through a file, tag, push, create the release object that triggers the archive webhook (only on the user's explicit request; irreversible); submit an explicit Software Heritage Save Code Now request and a Wayback Machine snapshot of the repository page (asynchronous, never block the release); sync the Hugging Face mirror via a separate `hf-sync` skill for repositories carrying `graph.jsonld`

Post-release: wait for DOI minting, write the new version DOI into the citation fields (`CITATION.cff`, README BibTeX and "How to cite"), leave the concept-DOI display links (README DOI badge, GitHub homepage field) untouched, retrieve the Software Heritage snapshot SWHID and record it in CITATION.cff (`identifiers`, `type: swh` — appended per release, never replaced), follow-up commit. On the first release of a new repository or paper, also include the record in the author's Zenodo community via the Zenodo API (per parent record; later versions inherit it). The skill does not self-register in community-governed records such as Wikidata (authorship-strategy ADR-0021). If opt-in lag caused the initial GitHub Release to skip Zenodo deposit, the recovery runbook deletes the tag and Release object and re-creates them after opt-in is enabled.

## Key concept

The concept DOI (parent record, latest-version-resolving) and the initial version DOI are typically issued as adjacent integers at first deposit. A user copying the citation snippet from the just-published version's UI page usually copies the wrong one. The skill separates the two by use: display links (README DOI badge, GitHub homepage field) carry the concept DOI and are set once; citation fields (`CITATION.cff`, BibTeX, "How to cite") carry the version DOI and change every release. The skill exists in part to prevent the sixteen-file drift incident that produced [ADR-0001 of the upstream research line](https://github.com/shimo4228/authorship-strategy/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-concept-doi-canonical.md) from recurring.

## Doctrine repository

- [authorship-strategy](https://github.com/shimo4228/authorship-strategy): the normative framework whose ADRs 0001-0003 (identifier-federation triplet) and ADR-0013 (intrinsic content-derived identifier layer) this skill instantiates as a release-time workflow

## Peer components

Other component skills of the same framework:

- [authorship-strategy-skill](https://github.com/shimo4228/authorship-strategy-skill): the framework as a skill a coding agent loads to weigh whether a plan fits the authorship strategy at all
- [llms-txt-writer](https://github.com/shimo4228/llms-txt-writer): operationalizes Layer 4 tactic 7's Answer.AI `llms.txt` convention; writes the llms.txt / llms-full.txt prose this skill does not write
- [jsonld-knowledge-graph](https://github.com/shimo4228/jsonld-knowledge-graph): operationalizes Layer 4 tactic 7's JSON-LD knowledge graph; designs the `graph.jsonld` that this runbook mirrors to Hugging Face

Terminology: *sibling* is reserved for research-line-level peers; at the component-skill level the term *peer component* is used.

## Related ecosystem skills

- [context-sync](https://github.com/shimo4228/context-sync): Phase 2 delegates drift detection to this skill

## Sibling research lines

The skill operates on artifacts in the author's research program; the author's hub [shimo4228](https://github.com/shimo4228/shimo4228) lists the five practice lines and their concept DOIs:

- [authorship-strategy](https://github.com/shimo4228/authorship-strategy) — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20263316
- [agent-knowledge-cycle (AKC)](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-knowledge-cycle) — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19200726
- [contemplative-agent](https://github.com/shimo4228/contemplative-agent) — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19212118

- [attention-not-self](https://github.com/shimo4228/attention-not-self) — DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20262112
